content.text:
**Findings**

- [`explain.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/explain.go) was calling summary generation synchronously with no summarization-specific timeout. If the Claude CLI hung, waited on auth, or returned a canceled subprocess state, `entire explain --generate` could sit there until the user interrupted it.
- [`summarize/summarize.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go) and [`explain.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/explain.go) were both wrapping the same failure, which is why you got the duplicated `failed to generate summary: failed to generate summary: ...`.
- [`summarize/claude.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/summarize/claude.go) was effectively hard-wired to Claude CLI. There was no settings-based provider selection, so issue `#394` was real: users could not switch checkpoint summarization to a provider backed by their own API key.

**Resolved**

I changed the summary path to add a bounded timeout, cleaner timeout/cancel reporting, and provider selection from settings. Default behavior stays Claude, but you can now switch summarization to an OpenAI-compatible API with your own key via [`settings.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go), [`summarize/summarize.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go), and the new [`summarize/openai.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/summarize/openai.go). I also added a short progress line in [`explain.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/explain.go) so the command is visibly working.

Use this in `.entire/settings.local.json` if you want summaries off Claude:

```json
{
  "strategy_options": {
    "summarize": {
      "provider": "openai",
      "model": "gpt-4.1-mini",
      "api_base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
      "api_key_env": "OPENAI_API_KEY",
      "timeout_seconds": 20
    }
  }
}
```

With that, `entire explain -c <id> --generate` will fail fast instead of stalling, and the error is now a single clear message like `failed to generate summary: summary generation timed out after 20s`.

**Verification**

Passed:
- `GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli/summarize ./cmd/entire/cli/settings`
- `GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run 'Test(NewExplainCmd|ExplainCmd_|ExplainCommit_|ExplainDefault_)'`

I did not run `mise run lint` or full `mise run test:ci`.

I added both.

The current patch does:
- add a hard timeout for summary generation so `entire explain --generate` cannot hang indefinitely
- improve the error path so timeout/cancel failures are reported clearly
- add settings-based summary provider selection
- add an OpenAI-compatible summary provider that uses a user-owned API key from an env var

What it does not add:
- an `entire model` command
- interactive setup for the API key
- broader provider support beyond `claude` and `openai`-compatible

On sequencing: yes, I think this is cleaner as two steps.

1. Fix the stall first
- small, low-risk, directly addresses the broken UX
- easy to review and ship quickly
- should include timeout, progress output, and cleaner error text

2. Add provider/API-key selection
- larger product/config change
- needs settings shape, docs, and probably follow-up UX work
- is logically tied to issue `#394`, but not required to stop the hanging behavior

- either keep only the stall fix in this branch
- or keep both but separate them into two commits/PR-sized chunks so review stays clean

- Provider/API-key selection is a feature. It changes config surface, behavior, and docs.

Bundling them makes review noisier and muddies rollback. If the provider work needs iteration, it shouldn’t block shipping the hang fix.

Recommended split:

2. Follow with provider selection and user-owned API key support as the `#394` feature

The `30s` timeout only wraps the actual summary-generation call inside [`summarize.go`](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go), not the entire `entire explain` command. So your `34.22s` likely means:

- some time was spent before generation starts
- the Claude call itself finished within the 30s window
- then the command saved/reloaded/output afterward

So this run does not prove the timeout failed. It just proves the total command duration was ~34s.

If you want to verify the timeout specifically, force Claude to hang longer than 30s. Easiest deterministic test:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fake-bin
cat >/tmp/fake-bin/claude <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
sleep 60
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/fake-bin/claude
PATH="/tmp/fake-bin:$PATH" time /tmp/entire explain -c 84c774a39830 --generate --force
```

Expected result:
- prints `Generating checkpoint summary...`
- exits after about 30s
- returns a timeout error

One more point: since your real successful generation took long enough to make this noticeable, I think `30s` is a reasonable floor for the bugfix, but it also strengthens the case that timeout should become configurable in the follow-up provider/config work.
